exposure: Fetal sacrococcygeal teratomas (SCTs) characteristics (tumor size, blood supply, shape, location)
outcome: Complications (increased fetal heart to chest ratio, fetal edema, placental edema, excessive/insufficient amniotic fluid, fetal distress, stillbirth, gestational diabetes mellitus, mirror syndrome, postpartum hemorrhage)
cohort: Pregnant women with fetal SCT (n=15) admitted to Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to January 2020
finding: Fetal SCT prognosis is closely correlated with tumor blood supply, growth rate, size, nature, clinical type, pathology, and maternal-fetal complications.
mod_finding: The timing and manner of the termination of pregnancy (induced delivery or cesarean section) should be determined on the basis of the pregnant female, the fetus, and the tumor.
